title: Asymptotic Inference for the Difference of Counterfactual Density Modes
banked_reason: The promised paired observable profile limit with n^-1/5 calibrated coverage is expressly unresolved; math and ten citations pass, but completed separate n^-1/3 kernel-Wald inference is incremental below the field floor.
gap_reasons: The promised paired observable profile limit with n^-1/5 calibrated coverage is expressly unresolved; this theorem instead supplies only n^-1/20 profile localization and finite-window simulation tracking, while a separate kernel-Wald procedure supplies the completed inference result.

The simulation bounds approximate the constructed Gaussian window distributions without establishing that they calibrate D_n, leaving global cancellation, whole-line stabilization and quantile identification unresolved.

The separate n^-1/3 Wald theorem is a finite-stratum extension of higher-order kernel mode inference, and its improvement over an earlier internal estimator establishes no published-method advance sufficient for field tier.
proof_attempt_summary: Four D0 rounds pursued weighted moving-mode outside-objective cancellation, then narrowed the unproved profile theorem honestly and developed a separate fourth-order signed-kernel Wald interval with n^-1/3 rate under the unchanged C4 model. D0.5 mathematics and all ten source checks passed, but the field contract remains undelivered and the final novelty grade is incremental. No F stages or Lean formalization ran; observable profile cancellation, whole-line localization, quantile regularity, coverage and n^-1/5 diameter remain open.
tldr: The target is the difference of two counterfactual marginal density modes. Under the unchanged finite-stratum model, an explicit fourth-order signed-kernel estimator with bandwidth \(n^{-1/9}\) has independent arm Gaussian limits at scale \(n^{1/3}\), feasible causal variance and a connected data-only Wald interval with fixed-law asymptotic \(95\%\) coverage and \(O_P(n^{-1/3})\) diameter. Original nuisance maps retain \(O_P(n^{-1/5})\) errors. The original profile retains its fixed-window oracle process law, connected inversion with \(O_P(n^{-1/20})\) localization and explicit simulation bounds. Weighted moving-profile cancellation and the observable whole-line law remain unresolved; the additional Gaussian procedure does not complete the paired-profile field contract. The original positive-kernel concentration lemma now covers only its unchanged nuisance maps; the established signed-kernel lemma supplies the additional estimator bounds.
gap: Ham--Westling--Doss provides pointwise causal density laws; Doss--Wellner provides fixed-null iid single-mode likelihood inference. Neither read theorem supplies the weighted moving-mode objective interface needed for a marginal modal contrast.
fill: The paired moving-mode objective law, its uniform outer-remainder estimate, and feasible strict inversion constitute the inference contribution. The quantitative finite-stratum restrictions are maintained regime choices, with explicit smooth heterogeneous members. Exact profile geometry and nuisance estimation are supporting machinery.
